Job Description Summary
Zum 01.08.2027 suchen wir eine/n weitere/n engagierte/n Auszubildende (m/w/d) zum Mechatroniker.
Du bist auf der Suche nach einer spannenden Ausbildung in einem internationalen Konzern mit guten Übernahmechancen? Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig!
Job Description
Wir bieten eine Ausbildung für jeden, der technisch und handwerklich vielfältig interessiert ist und immer schon mal "hoch hinaus" wollte. Bei uns lernst du in 3,5 Jahren alles über die Zusammenhänge Mechanik, Elektro- sowie Steuerungstechnik und setzt dich mit unserer umfangreichen Anlagentechnologie auseinander. Das mechatronische System Windkraftanlage bietet hierfür die idealen Voraussetzungen. In einer Vielzahl von verschiedenen internen und externen Ausbildungsrotationen werden die umfangreichen Lehrinhalte vermittelt. Die Rotationen reichen von der Fertigung über die Qualitätsprüfung, Arbeitsvorbereitung bis hin zum Service der installierten Anlage im Feld. Gemeinsam mit unseren qualifizierten Facharbeitern unterstützt du die hohen Qualitätsanforderungen der Windindustrie.
Das bringst du mit:
Fachoberschulreife / Sekundarabschluss I
Ausgeprägtes Interesse für technische Zusammenhänge und gutes mathematisches Verständnis
Handwerkliche Begeisterung sowie technisches Geschick
Gute Deutsch- und Mathematikkenntnisse
Interesse in einem großen Team zu arbeiten
Idealerweise Vorkenntnisse aus einem Berufsgrundschuljahr (Elektrotechnik/Mechanik) oder Praxiserfahrungen durch Praktika und/oder Nebenjobs oder Ähnliches
Vielfalt, Integration und Gleichberechtigung sind das Herzstück unser Unternehmenskultur. Bei uns ist jeder willkommen – also bewirb dich jetzt!
Job description
We are looking for another committed trainee (m/f/d) to become a mechatronics engineer from August 1st, 2027.
Are you looking for exciting training in an international company with good chances of being taken on? Then you've come to the right place!
We offer training for anyone who has a wide range of technical and craft interests and has always wanted to “aim high”. With us, in 3.5 years you will learn everything about the connections between mechanics, electrical and control technology and get to know our extensive system technology. The mechatronic wind turbine system offers the ideal conditions for this. The extensive teaching content is conveyed in a variety of different internal and external training rotations. The rotations range from production to quality inspection, work preparation and service of the installed system in the field. Together with our qualified skilled workers, you support the high quality requirements of the wind industry.
Requirements:
Technical college entrance qualification/secondary qualification I
Strong interest in technical contexts and good mathematical understanding
Enthusiasm for craftsmanship and technical skill
Good knowledge of German and mathematics
Interested in working in a large team
Ideally, previous knowledge from a year of vocational school (electrical engineering/mechanics) or practical experience through internships and/or part-time jobs or similar
Diversity, inclusion and equality are at the heart of our corporate culture. Everyone is welcome here – so apply now!
Additional Information
Relocation Assistance Provided: No

We operate with a founder’s mindset. We deliver innovation with passion, speed, and courage. We continuously challenge our thinking and are empowered to dream big and take smart risks.
What impact you’ll make
GE Vernova is preparing to introduce a robotic manufacturing cell for 145 kV high-voltage circuit breaker production. A successful launch depends on more than the robot: processes, material structures, SAP data, MES orchestration, operator workflows, and production readiness must all align. In this role, you will map current and future-state workflows, check that BOM and material allocation structures can support robotic operations, evaluate the interfaces among HERMES, SAP, and robotic equipment, and help assemble the readiness assessment and action plan the team will use to move toward implementation. You will work across manufacturing, controls, and systems teams and see how an automation project comes together beyond the equipment itself.
Job Description
What you’ll do (Job Responsibilities)
Analyze existing manufacturing processes and the proposed robotic operations for 145 kV circuit breaker production.
Map current-state and future-state workflows, including material flow, operator tasks, and handoffs.
Verify that BOM and material allocation structures meet robotic manufacturing requirements, and document gaps.
Support MES orchestration and integration planning for the robotic cell.
Evaluate the interfaces among HERMES, SAP, and robotic equipment and summarize requirements and risks.
Collaborate with manufacturing teams to identify the process changes needed for robotic production.
Develop standardized work instructions and transition documentation for operators and support staff.
Support automation readiness reviews, equipment testing, and validation activities where feasible.
Identify risks to cell implementation, recommend mitigations, and compile an implementation action plan.
What you’ll bring (Basic Qualifications)
Current enrollment in an undergraduate or graduate degree program in mechanical, electrical, mechatronics, robotics, industrial or systems engineering, or a related discipline.
Coursework or project experience in robotics, automation, mechatronics, or manufacturing systems.
Experience creating technical documentation, process maps, or CAD models through coursework or projects.
Ability to work with cross-functional teams and communicate technical information clearly.
Must have the ability to work in the US for an unlimited amount of time without sponsorship.
What will make you stand out (Desired Qualifications)
Experience with PLCs or industrial control systems.
Experience with industrial robot programming, simulation, or robotic cell design.
Familiarity with CAD tools and layout or fixture design.
Exposure to SAP, MES, or other manufacturing data systems.
Familiarity with machine safety concepts or standards relevant to robotic cells.
Experience with process engineering, lean methods, or risk assessment tools such as FMEA.
Hands-on manufacturing, lab, or prior internship experience.

What impact you’ll make
Many of our high-voltage dead tank circuit breaker orders match, or closely resemble, configurations we have engineered before, yet each one still requires engineers to rebuild BOMs and drawings by hand. In this role, you will analyze historical order data, define which designs qualify as repeatable, and build a working prototype that automates the path from BOM generation to drawing creation. Your work will help free engineering capacity for new design challenges, with a target of reducing engineering cycle time by 70% for qualifying repeat customer jobs, and will leave the team a documented foundation for future deployment.

What you’ll do (Job Responsibilities)
Analyze historical customer orders, BOMs, and drawings to identify and categorize repeat and near-repeat designs.
Develop a repeatability classification method, with clear criteria for which jobs qualify for automation.
Measure baseline engineering cycle times for a representative set of repeat jobs.
Map the current engineering workflow and identify the manual activities best suited to automation.
Build a functional prototype that automates BOM generation through engineering drawing creation, using Python, CAD automation, and system APIs as appropriate.
Validate automated outputs against engineering requirements in review sessions with design engineers.
Measure achieved productivity gains against the baseline, working toward a 70% cycle-time reduction target for qualifying repeat jobs.
Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing technology, and IT partners to align the prototype with product configuration, CAD, and SAP workflows.
Document the solution, assumptions, and limitations to support future deployment, and present results to engineering leadership.

Current enrollment in an undergraduate or graduate degree program in mechanical, electrical, computer science, industrial or systems engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Programming experience (such as Python) demonstrated through coursework, research, or projects.
Coursework or project experience working with structured data, CAD models, or engineering documentation such as BOMs and drawings.
Experience documenting and presenting technical work through coursework, projects, or prior roles.
Must have the ability to work in the US for an unlimited amount of time without sponsorship.
What will make you stand out (Desired Qualifications)
Experience with CAD automation or scripting, such as Creo or another parametric CAD tool.
Familiarity with APIs, databases, or data pipelines used to connect engineering systems.
Exposure to BOM structures, PLM or ERP systems (such as SAP), or product configurators.
Experience with process mapping, cycle-time analysis, or lean methods.
Familiarity with electrical CAD, such as E3.series.
Interest in rule-based or knowledge-based engineering and design automation.

We operate with a founder’s mindset. We deliver innovation with passion, speed, and courage. We continuously challenge our thinking and are empowered to dream big and take smart risks.
What impact you’ll make
Smooth assembly starts with the right component at the right workstation. When engineering BOMs and manufacturing routings do not consistently allocate components to the stations that consume them, the result is kitting errors, material shortages, unnecessary movement, and production interruptions. In this role, you will extract and analyze BOM data, connect it to actual workstation consumption, and propose improved SAP component allocation and routing structures for a selected mechanical assembly bay. Your work will target a 25% reduction in material-related eAndons in that bay and will define the structured data that future AGV and robotic material delivery will depend on.
Job Description
What you’ll do (Job Responsibilities)
Develop a repeatable method to extract and analyze BOM data from engineering and enterprise databases using SQL and Python.
Evaluate the component varieties and quantities used at individual workstations in a selected mechanical assembly bay.
Map engineering BOM components to actual manufacturing consumption locations and identify allocation inconsistencies.
Analyze historical material-related eAndons to establish a baseline and identify leading causes.
Identify kitting opportunities that reduce shortages, errors, and unnecessary material movement.
Propose optimized SAP BOM structures and routing assignments in collaboration with manufacturing engineering, supply chain, and SAP experts.
Define data-structure requirements so proposed structures can support future AGV and robotic material delivery.
Support engineering data integration between Genesis product configuration and SAP.
Document findings, support a pilot of the recommendations, and measure results against a 25% reduction target for material-related eAndons in the selected bay.
What you’ll bring (Basic Qualifications)
Current enrollment in an undergraduate or graduate degree program in industrial or systems engineering, mechanical engineering, data science, operations, or a related discipline.
Experience analyzing data with SQL, Python, or similar tools, demonstrated through coursework or projects.
Coursework or project experience in manufacturing systems, operations, supply chain, or materials management.
Ability to explain technical findings clearly to engineering, operations, and supply chain audiences.
Must have the ability to work in the US for an unlimited amount of time without sponsorship.
What will make you stand out (Desired Qualifications)
Exposure to SAP, particularly BOM, routing, or materials management modules.
Understanding of BOM structures, routings, and how they drive production planning.
Experience with kitting, line balancing, material flow, or lean manufacturing concepts.
Experience building dashboards or reports with tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
Interest in automated material delivery, including AGVs and robotic assembly.
Experience working with large, imperfect datasets and resolving data-quality issues.

HERMES, our manufacturing execution system, went live in September 2026, and consistent use on the shop floor is now essential to production data quality and to future automation. In this role, you will examine how HERMES is used across production areas and shifts, uncover the usability, integration, and data barriers that affect it, from barcode scanner placement to SAP master data to serialization, and help implement practical improvements with operators and the HERMES team. Your work will support a goal of 100% operator utilization of MES job clocking within a defined project scope, produce dashboards that make performance visible, and define the MES readiness requirements for robotic manufacturing.

Analyze HERMES adoption data by production area and shift to establish a baseline for operator job clocking.
Interview operators and supervisors to identify the barriers to consistent clocking and recommend solutions.
Improve shop floor barcode scanner placement, fixturing, and usability through trials and operator feedback.
Evaluate SAP master data and integration issues that affect MES performance and recommend corrections.
Develop best practices for quality documentation management and product serialization in HERMES.
Support Genesis product configuration integration where it affects MES workflows.
Build operational reports and dashboards from MES data using tools such as Power BI, SQL, or Python.
Support multi-site and multi-shift deployment activities, including training and communication materials.
Define MES readiness requirements for future robotic manufacturing, and track progress toward a goal of 100% operator job clocking within the defined project scope.

Current enrollment in an undergraduate or graduate degree program in industrial or systems engineering, electrical, mechanical, computer science, data science, or a related discipline.
Experience analyzing data with SQL, Python, or similar tools, demonstrated through coursework or projects.
Coursework or project experience in manufacturing, operations, process improvement, or information systems.
Ability to gather feedback from and communicate clearly with shop floor and technical audiences.
Must have the ability to work in the US for an unlimited amount of time without sponsorship.
What will make you stand out (Desired Qualifications)
Exposure to MES or ERP systems, such as HERMES or SAP.
Experience building dashboards with Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools.
Interest in human-centered design, usability, or human factors.
Experience with lean, Six Sigma, or other process improvement methods.
Understanding of product serialization, traceability, or quality documentation.
Experience with industrial systems integration or data interfaces between enterprise and shop floor systems.
Experience with change management, training, or user adoption projects.

What impact you’ll make
Operators who assemble low-voltage control cabinets for high-voltage circuit breakers interpret dense wiring drawings and manually highlight wire gauges and other critical details before they can wire. That process adds avoidable mental effort, presents information inconsistently, and contributes to wiring errors and rework. In this role, you will study how drawings are used on the shop floor, establish a reliable first-pass yield baseline, and prototype clearer drawing presentation and digital work instructions, beginning with 362 kV low-voltage control cabinets. You will pilot your ideas with production operators and work with DFx, offshore manufacturing, and training teams so the results can extend to other cabinet and product types.

Quantify the manual highlighting and drawing-interpretation effort for representative 362 kV cabinet jobs.
Establish a baseline for true first-pass yield (FPY) and rework frequency.
Analyze recurring wiring errors and rework records to identify documentation-related root causes.
Develop an automated wire gauge highlighting or improved drawing presentation prototype using E3.series, Python, or comparable tools.
Evaluate alternative visual and digital work instruction formats and recommend a preferred approach.
Pilot improvements with production operators, gather their feedback, and measure resulting changes in FPY and rework.
Partner with DFx, offshore manufacturing, and training teams to draft standardized operating procedures for applicable cabinet and product types.
Present findings, pilot results, and next-step recommendations to engineering and manufacturing leaders.
